title: Kabeer Biswas’ M Raises $9 Mn Led By RTP Global
summary: Dunzo founder Kabeer Biswas raises $9 million for AI startup M
detailed: AI startup M, founded by Dunzo cofounder Kabeer Biswas and Kartik Mishra, raised $9 million (Rs 82 crore) in a funding round led by RTP Global.
Existing investors Peak XV Partners and Blume Ventures also participated, bringing the startup's total capital raised to approximately $20 million.
The fresh funding follows an $11 million seed round raised seven months prior, building on an early rollout that served about 150 households in Bengaluru.
This matters because Biswas is attempting to pioneer a new consumer tech category focused on AI-powered home management and routine automation for affluent households.
sentences: Dunzo cofounder Kabeer Biswas’ AI startup M has raised $9 Mn (₹82 Cr) in a fresh funding round led by VC firm RTP Global, sources familiar with the development told Inc42.
Existing investors of the startup, including Peak XV Partners and Blume Ventures, also doubled down on their erstwhile bets.
With this fundraise, M’s total capital raised has reached around $20 Mn.
Queries sent to M, RTP Global, and Blume Ventures didn’t receive any response till the time of publication.
The story would be updated based on receiving their responses.
The latest round comes around seven months after M raised $11 Mn (around ₹102 Cr) in a seed funding round led by Peak XV, with participation from Blume Ventures and fintech major CRED.
Founded in December 2025 by Biswas and former Swish executive Kartik Mishra, M currently offers access through a waitlist.

Details of its services remain scant, but the startup had earlier said it planned to weave AI “into the most human part of a home — the kitchen” to help people manage their homes by automating routine decisions, coordination, and everyday services.
“We will make modern living feel frictionless and fundamentally transformed,” M’s description of itself reads.
In June, M was reported to be serving around 150 households in Bengaluru as part of its early rollout.
The startup was also exploring a subscription-led model, with its target audience comprising affluent urban households.
Biswas, who cofounded hyperlocal delivery startup Dunzo in 2014, launched M after a brief stint with Flipkart Minutes.
Dunzo, which had raised capital from Reliance Retail, shut its operations in 2025.
The Bengaluru-based startup struggled with mounting cash burn, operational challenges and competition in the quick commerce market.
Biswas subsequently joined Flipkart in 2025 to lead its quick commerce business, Minutes, but exited the company in October that year.
With M, Biswas is attempting to build a new consumer tech category around AI-powered household management, moving beyond the delivery-led convenience model that defined his earlier venture.
